annotation.title_clean: Ethics and Robot Democratization: Reflecting on Integrative Ethics Practices
annotation.title_en: Ethics and Robot Democratization: Reflecting on Integrative Ethics Practices
annotation.summary_en: Journal article reflecting on an interdisciplinary project to "democratize" collaborative robots, using the author's observations to argue for integrative robot ethics. It proposes three components: a clearer definition of interdisciplinarity, the role of ethical critique, and richer anticipatory concepts, while noting concerns about ethics washing.
key_provisions_or_claims: Integrating ethics into robot development, design and implementation is vital for maturing robot ethics as a field.
Ethical approaches risk being toothless or 'ethics washing' without continuous critique.
Three components for integrative ethics: interdisciplinarity, ethical critique, anticipatory concepts.
Case study of a cobot democratization project involving industry, academia and non-profit partners.
Value-based frameworks such as Participatory Design and Value Sensitive Design are useful for robot design.
